questions.title: Python (SEN Holiday Practise 2026 Q32)
questions.label: SEN Holiday Practise 2026 Q32
questions.stimulus:
A local food delivery business operates in a busy suburban area and partners with several independent restaurants. Customers place orders through the business’s website, selecting multiple food items from a menu. Each item has a fixed price, and the system calculates the total cost of the order before payment.

To encourage larger orders, the business offers a 10% discount when the total order value exceeds $30.

The system must calculate the total, apply the discount where appropriate, and display a clear summary for both customers and staff.

parts.prompt:
A customer places an order containing several food items. The prices of the items are stored in the list below: prices = \[12.50, 8.00, 5.75\]

Write a Python program that calculates and prints the total cost of the order.

marking_criteria.criterion: Correct Python statement producing correct output
Minor syntax or logic error

parts.prompt:
The business wants to automate order processing.

Write a Python function called process\_order() that calculates the total cost of the order, applying a 10% discount if the total is greater than $30.

The function should take the following parameters: customer\_name, and prices. It should return the final amount payable.

Other requirements:

• Use meaningful variable names

• Apply the discount only when the condition is met

• Round the final cost to 2 decimal places

Output should be printed in the format below:

Customer: Alex  
Final cost: $27.45

marking_criteria.criterion:
Provides a complete and correct Python solution that:
• defines the function correctly with appropriate parameters
• correctly calculates the total cost
• correctly applies the discount condition
• formats and displays the output correctly
• uses readable code that meets all question requirements
Provides a mostly correct Python solution with one minor error or omission, such as a small formatting issue or minor syntax issue.
Provides a generally correct solution that calculates the total and attempts the discount condition, but contains an error in logic, output, or structure.
Provides a partial solution that shows some understanding of the required calculation, but the function, discount condition, or output is incomplete.
Provides limited Python code that includes one or two relevant elements, but does not meet most of the question requirements.
Provides a minimal attempt with little relevant Python code or limited understanding of the task.

parts.sample_answer:
def process\_order(customer\_name, prices):

    total = sum(prices)

    if total > 30:

        total \*= 0.9

    total = round(total, 2)

    print(f"Customer: {customer\_name}")

    print(f"Final cost: ${total}")

    return total
